m2-treatment.title: Run the TREATMENT arm live: headless claude -p, parent claims its own spine, subagents A/B/C plus a nested dispatch
m2-treatment.imperative: Launch a fresh headless `claude -p ... --settings <abs treatment settings> --allowedTools Bash Task Agent --permission-mode acceptEdits --model sonnet` with cwd inside sb-treatment. The parent claims its own spine, dispatches subagent A (many corpus chunks), subagent B (deliberately fewer chunks), subagent C (claims nothing), and subagent D which itself dispatches a nested subagent E. Each claiming agent runs the engine's `current` between chunks and reports it VERBATIM, then attempts `advance` and reports VERBATIM whatever comes back; at least one releases. The agents are NOT told what a trip is, what output to expect, or what number to reach. Capture the full stdout with its real exit code, the sandbox binding store, every gauge.json (or a listing recording its absence), and copies of every agent transcript.

m3-pairing.imperative: Write a recomputation script that, for EACH claiming agent id, recomputes fill from that agent's OWN agent-<id>.jsonl and asserts it equals the fill_fraction in the gauge.json sitting in the spine directory that the SAME id's binding key points at. Assert also: key shape <uuid>#<hex>; the parent's key is bare; the two agents' fills DIFFER; observed_at does not predate the agent's first chunk read; identity_resolution_ms is inside the 100ms budget; the released agent's composite key is gone while the parent's survives; the non-claiming subagent wrote nothing; and the nested-dispatch outcome is recorded either way. Exit non-zero if the pairing does not hold 2 of 2.

why_trail.why: Handoff complete on all eight fields. Mechanism understood: HARD trip needs fill>=0.15 on a 1M-window model, gauge.json written per PostToolUse into the spine dir the binding key points at, and advance refuses via _trip_hard_gate. Control arm is genuinely pre-fix: main checkout has zero binding_key occurrences.

Sandbox built outside the repo. 20 chunks / 1,921,073 bytes of prose per arm; 8 gated spines (4 per arm, 2 gates each) all validated by this worktree's engine, exit 0, ACTIVE g1. Gates are why_exempt with a trivially-true command postcondition so the ONLY thing that can refuse an advance is the trip. Both sandboxes' binding stores and harness project dirs confirmed absent before the run.

Treatment arm ran twice. Run 1 (archived under run1/) already fired the HARD trip but a PowerShell-only exit-code suffix in my prompt blocked BRAVO and ECHO from claiming at all; harness fixed, sandboxes rebuilt, run 2 clean. Run 2: parent bare key + 2 composite keys, four distinct readings 0.329482 / 0.102211 / 0.064216 / 0.094663, wk-alpha advance REFUSED at 33%. BRAVO's authored report was blocked by a classifier at its final message, so its raw commands and results are recovered verbatim from its own transcript instead.

recompute.py parses each agent-<id>.jsonl from scratch (the hook under test is never imported) and pins the comparison to the gauge's own observed_at, which also makes the anti-crossing test direct: a crossed reading would name a moment absent from that agent's transcript. 2 of 2 paired exactly (0.329482 and 0.102211, token-for-token), parent 0.094663, nested depth-2 agent 0.064216, all four NOT CROSSED, identity_resolution_ms 0.078-0.084ms, exit 0.

Control arm ran the byte-identical script with one variable: settings name the MAIN checkout's hooks. Result is the pre-fix blindness exactly: one bare key holding 3 spines, zero readings for any dispatched agent, ambiguous-binding skip sidecars at all four paths, no trip anywhere, every advance succeeded. My first control assertion overclaimed 'no reading anywhere' and failed: the parent DOES get one reading in the 31s window before the first subagent claims, then it freezes at 4.77% for the rest of the run. Corrected to that measured invariant. Control ALPHA independently reached 0.329265 -- the same context as treatment ALPHA's 0.329482 -- and advanced unimpeded.

49 evidence files plus both transcript sets (1.8MB each arm) archived under evidence/g4-*; IMPLEMENTER_RESULT written with the verdict, all five close criteria, all eight named falsifiers checked, both arms' real command output and exit codes, the two fill numbers side by side, what was deliberately not done, three triage candidates and honest workflow feedback.
